items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Just true playing in the Pierron band... I made Pierron get the old man, see, because he was the style drummer we needed in that band

ctx.x: Well Lewis was a baby when I was playing with his daddy.
I mean the old man. The old man? Yeah, how did you meet him? Well, that's true.

He's much older than me, you know. Just true playing in the Pierron band. You see, Bill used to play drums with us, you know, Pierron. Bill, what was that? Bill, Matthews, the trombone player? Uh huh. So when Bill left, I don't know why he left, but anyway, I made Pierron get the old man, see, because he was the style drummer we needed in that band, see.

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Well then I played violin with them, with Eagle Band, see.

ctx.x: Remember the drummer? Yeah. Put it off a minute. Peter Pocosch, 6th of February 1962, tape 3. I guess you're about one of the oldest playing musicians around, trumpet players. Can you remember any of the old time guys like Buddy Bolden and Whitman? Oh yeah.

I remember Buddy. I was quite young though. He died young too. He was an old fellow when he died. He must have been in his thirties, you know? What kind of trumpet playing did you make? Well he was mostly a blues player, you know? Mostly blues. He mostly make tunes, you know, like a pallet on the floor or blues and things like that. That's mostly the type of band they had, you know? Well he'd play jobs, you know? He'd play jobs, you know.

No, I mean would he play a job, you know? He'd play a job, you know? No, I mean would he play trumpet all the time when they were playing that number or would he let down and let the other instruments solo?
